whatChanged: no GLB bytes changed this round — the diagnosis (below) is the deliverable; the round's defined successful outcome ("the gradient enters at stage X and cannot be removed without Y"). The only code change is the committed U_BAND stage instrument in materialize_mpfb_humanoid_candidate.py (print-only; verified byte-identical bake: shipped vs instrumented skin texture sha 217526385f62, 653719 B, scalpPrims=0).

stageReport.method: in-bake instrument in apply_texture_mask_hairline — for each U band over the SAME dome loops the planted hair-covers-both-sides test samples (>= 0.94 H, |x| > 5 mm), the fraction whose OWN poly is scalp (region), whose UV texel is white in the raster mask (raster), white in the Cycles mask bake (bake), and hair in the composite (final), plus face-band and below-hairline membership

diagnosis.whereTheGradientEnters: the per-polygon REGION at composite time (the scalp material state already includes the round-5 face-front unpaint below hairline_z and the round-8 seam snap) plus a small COMPOSITE addition (the face-band level set, ~5 pts in the far-U band). The raster reproduces the region exactly; the mask bake tracks it (its small extra bias does not feed the composite — round 14); the skin bake carries no hair at all (scalp polys swapped to skin for the bake). None of the three candidates (texel-density gradient, bake-margin, UV-frame classifier) is the cause.
diagnosis.whatTheFarUBandIs: the dome's base ring at the FACE FRONT: avgZfrac 0.948 (aisha) is below the derived hairline 0.9715 H, so the face-band portion (42.6%) is the forehead — legitimately skin below the accepted round-5 hairline. The back/mid portion of the band is hair. World-space split (shipped bytes): dome front = 28% hair, back = 100%, mid = 100%; |x|>0.06 = 100%, |x|<=0.03 = 27%. The bare region is the face-front strip (y <= forehead plane) — the forehead.
diagnosis.whyTheInstrumentSeesIt: the round-14 dome band (>= 0.94 H) and the round-10 hairline (0.9715 H) overlap by ~3 cm. The U-axis of the crown UV strip runs down the head (top-of-crown at low U, hairline at high U), so the hairline boundary projects across the whole U range of the strip and the sample reads it as monotone thinning. This contradicts the handback's 'NOT a world-space pattern' — it IS world-space (face-front bare, back/mid hair); the U-correlation is the UV wrap of the face-front strip.
diagnosis.correction: the orchestrator's round-16 'world-centre verts span the entire U range (0.641-0.812) at 33%/26% hair' is reproduced and explained: the near-midline face-front dome verts (the forehead below the hairline) map across the whole crown strip in U.
diagnosis.cannotBeRemovedWithout: moving the hairline height (the round-5 derived, round-10-refused known-good column) or painting the forehead (widening the region — refused this round, and ineffective: the composite's face-band level set unpaints the face front below the hairline regardless of the region). The far-U band is the hairline, not a texture or bake defect.

sideFindings.id: side-scalp band never fires on MPFB heads
sideFindings.measured: apply_mesh_native_scalp_hair_material_region derives max_scalp_half_width from the BODY x-span (0.16 + 0.65*0.018 = 0.1717 x width): aisha bodyWidth 0.993 m -> maxHw 0.1704 m; head half-width at the crown is ~0.075 m. The side-scalp band [0.55*maxHw, 1.05*maxHw] = [0.094, 0.179] lies outside the head, so the head's sides at 0.90-0.935 H are never scalp (bare temples above the ears). On the Anny rail the body width is ~0.45 m so the band fires; the MPFB path (arms-span width ~0.99 m) misses the head entirely.
sideFindings.verdict: real region defect on the MPFB path, BELOW the dome band (0.90-0.935 H) — out of this round's subject; reported not fixed

sideFindings.id: child's hair cap is proportionally half the adults'
sideFindings.measured: hairlineFrac 0.9758 (child) vs 0.9715/0.9699 (aisha/nurse); cap = (1-hairlineFrac) x H = 3.0 cm (child, 1.241 m) vs 4.7/5.3 cm (aisha/nurse, 1.666/1.760 m). The child's head is a larger fraction of the body (anny reference 0.160 vs 0.100), so a body-height-derived hairline yields a head-relative cap of ~12-15% vs the adults' ~22-25%. This is the round-6-anticipated column-heuristic degeneracy on the child's proportions.
sideFindings.verdict: reported with the measurement per round 6 ('report it with the measurement rather than forcing a pass'); NOT fixed (moving the hairline is the refused known-good column)
